subject: Request: Proof of key wrapping and in-transit protections for SOC2 review
messages:
From: Alice Bruner <alice.bruner@zenwave.health>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: SOC2-Audit <SOC2-Audit@clearadvisors.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Proof of key wrapping and in-transit protections for SOC2 review

Hi Tessa,

We're in the middle of our SOC 2 readiness window and ClearAdvisors has asked for specific evidence around how Redwood protects keys in transit and at rest. Could you provide the following artifacts or point us to where they can be downloaded?

- HSM attestation that shows FIPS/CC compliance and attestation date (most recent).
- Key wrapping flow diagram that covers both BYOK and Redwood-managed keys (include where wrapping/unwrapping happens).
- Key rotation policy and rotation logs for the last 90 days for the tenant key used during our POC.
- Confirmation of TLS cipher suites and whether application-level envelope encryption is used for file stores.

We aim to bundle these into the SOC package by Thursday EOD. If there are smaller artifacts you can share now (e.g., attestation PDF) that would help.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Bruner
Director, InfoSec
ZenWave Health

---
Note: attaching our audit checklist as reference (not included here).

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Bruner <alice.bruner@zenwave.health>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Proof of key wrapping and in-transit protections for SOC2 review

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Irene (security/compliance) and Marissa (ops) to pull the artifacts. Quick answers up front while we collect the files:

- We can provide the HSM attestation PDF (latest: 2028-06-30) and will include the FIPS references.
- Key wrapping: we use envelope encryption. KMS hosts tenant DEKs which are wrapped by a master KEK stored in HSM. For BYOK customers we perform an import operation where the customer wraps their key under our HSM-wrapped KEK and we store only wrapped blobs.
- Rotation: rotation policy is documented and we can export rotation events (audit log entries) for the last 90 days.
- TLS: our platform enforces TLS1.3 for in-transit; listed cipher suites are in our transport diagram. Application-layer envelope encryption is used for object stores containing sensitive payloads.

I'll attach: kms_key_rotation_plan_v2.pdf (rotation policy + schedule), hsm_attestation_2028-06-30.pdf. Marissa will include the transport-layer-diagram.png and a filtered rotation log extract.

Target: IRENE — can you confirm whether we should redact any internal hostnames before sending the rotation logs to ZenWave?

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: kms_key_rotation_plan_v2.pdf]
[Attachment: hsm_attestation_2028-06-30.pdf]

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Bruner <alice.bruner@zenwave.health>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Proof of key wrapping and in-transit protections for SOC2 review

Hi all,

Thanks — I pulled the requested artifacts and prepared a filtered rotation log extract that removes internal instance IDs and full principal ARNs. The extract includes: timestamp, key_id (redwood-kms-xxxx), rotation_event (rotate/import), actor_role (Ops/AutomatedRotation), and checksum of wrapped DEK blob.

Attached: transport-layer-diagram.png (shows TLS1.3 enforced at ingress and inter-service mTLS in internal fabric) and rotation_events_filtered.csv. For clarity: rotation_events_filtered.csv is an audit log export in CSV format — we removed internal hostnames and IPs but left tenant key identifiers to map to your POC tenant. If you need the full unredacted logs for your auditor, we can arrange transfer under an encrypted link and NDA.

Two quick notes:
- BYOK import is a customer-initiated WrapUnderKek operation that we log as import events; the private key material never leaves the customer's environment unwrapped.
- HSM attestation is signed by our vendor and includes module serial numbers; if the auditor needs OEM-signed chain-of-trust metadata, we can request the vendor bundle (takes 48–72h).

Lauren — please confirm the retention window shown in rotation_events_filtered.csv (I had it set to 120 days for the export).

Regards,
Irene Choi
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: transport-layer-diagram.png]
[Attachment: rotation_events_filtered.csv]

From: SOC2-Audit <SOC2-Audit@clearadvisors.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Alice Bruner <alice.bruner@zenwave.health>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Proof of key wrapping and in-transit protections for SOC2 review

Hi Irene / Tessa,

Received the attachments; high-level confirmation that these artifacts look appropriate for our SOC2 evidence bundle. A couple of follow-ups before we close the ticket:

1) The rotation_events_filtered.csv includes the rotation events but we need a short mapping document that links the redwood-kms-xxxx IDs to the tenant POC key id shown in our earlier questionnaire. Can you provide a single-page mapping (no hostnames) that ties the identifiers together?

2) Please confirm whether the HSM attestation includes the cryptographic module firmware versions — auditors will sometimes request the exact firmware string. If not present, provide your ETA for vendor-signed firmware details.

If you can send those two items by EOD tomorrow, we should be able to mark the KMS/HSM section as reviewed. Thanks — great responsiveness.

Cheers,
Sam Patel
Senior Auditor, ClearAdvisors
